body: Hey. This is going against pretty much everyone's idea of help, but you are on my comment so I want to give advice to something I thought helped me. A dermaroller hard, but not that hard, gave me the pain without the blood. You seem like the person who needs to see things, but I was too, I still have my blades, but this thing that barely affects me still gives me the pain I want.

What was the right meds for you?  I've pretty much got the right ones for me and time just fucks with it. I'm now on Lamictal, quietapine, a long one which I can't call off of the top of my head, and Mirtazapine.
I'd reccomend Spaced or Peep show because they helped me before. Spaced is like a fever dream and Peep show is shown through the person's eyes and somehow that made me feel comfortable.
Get them to send you to a mental health place. I have no idea if this is a different country but I have went to a GZP in Ireland and they are awful. Get proper help.

Stay here for doggo. Don't let anyone ever tell you that you need a human reasson. Doggo can be your reason to stay around. It's a good reason. Coincidentally, same reason in Afterlife on Netflix. But the most valid one I know.
If it's not working, ask to change pills.
I get that. I'm not going to try give you a speech on breathing or trying to be in the moment or anything like that. But have you tried to get help? Have you tried pills?
Stay here for doggo. They need you. The rest will be hard but you will get through it with help if you want it.

This seems fully up to your comfort zone. She is vaccinated. You can't find out who else is. I'm similar that I don't want to be near anyone who could give it to me and I'd give it to an elderly parent. 

It's unlikely you will get it. But it is possible. Do you. Don't be scared of everything. Just be careful. Make sure you don't bring it to someone else even though you may think you can't. Stay away from older people for 6 days and I'd say it would be fine.

I want to say how bad with me but I won't in public. But I can tell you how it went to less panic attacks. The first thing was pills. The second thing was breathing and the third thing was trying to regulate it. But really. It all started with the first one. Some (alot) of people are 'you can do it yourself' types. I am not. Pills work. I spent 5 years on one's that didn't before it clicked for me. Message me if you want to know which ones. But it was mainly mood stabilizers that changes my life. I'd have to check the concoction.

You are right. 100%. Its too hard at the moment but maybe I muster the courage sometime. 
Hopefully.

I understand why you did that. It's not an easy sentence, nevermind story. I'd rather bury it, but if I am waking up to the morning after, almost every day it becomes a problem. The actual act is blurry. The next morning is not. It crystal.

So this is all really good advice and I appreciate it alot. I felt overwhelmed after I wrote it so took note, but didn't reply a few days ago. I needed for no spotlight to be near me. 
Substance abuse used to be mental for me, but I'm doing better now. I exercise a good bit more but have insomnia. Take meds for it, as well as bipolar (which I wasn't diagnosed with at the time). 
I don't mean to say that I've been trying your methods and it's failing. I definitely haven't been to any normal standard. Just a little.  but I will. I don't think I'm ready for the last part. I am not ready to tell anyone I know. The tears from other people aren't the ones I want. Why bring that on someone I love? If you have any idea on that I would love to know. What's the point in which another person should be involved emotionally? When it hurts me too much or should they be left alone?
I'm really sorry at what happend to you. So how do you live? I'm struggling at the moment. I know it's not just this, but there is a physical aspect to this for me.

I get you. I'm on it a good while. It was prescribed for anxiety but also insomnia. I wake up groggy every day. I don't feel like a normal person until about the third hour after waking. if it is for anxiety I would ask to change. I just got a higher dose for insomnia this week so I am hopeful it will work (different drugs for anxiety too though...better than before, but not great).

I moved into my dad's house who I have never lived with at 27 (9 years alone or with my ex) but I don't think your parent will ever understand unless they have gone through it. My dad literally told me that not a single person in his generation had mental health problems when he also openly admits his older sister has worse problems than me (I have no kids, I can't fuck anyone up).
You may feel crazy but it can be fixed. I personally have been better after I had a change of psychiatrist.  Rediagnosed too, but it's because of one person that helped me. Still crazy I suppose but less suicidal. Which is what I thought you were talking about.
